subject: Food Science
title: Water Quality
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Water Quality.

hook.text: Contaminated water used to wash lettuce caused a Cyclospora outbreak across 14 US states in 2018.

buildup.text: Water is used in food production for washing, processing, cooling, and as an ingredient. Contaminated water taints everything.

discovery.text: Irrigation with untreated wastewater spreads E. coli and parasites to fresh produce—lettuce, spinach, berries absorb pathogens.

twist.text: Ice is a food. Ice machines are rarely cleaned properly and can harbor Listeria, mold, and biofilms inside.

climax.text: The FDA's Produce Safety Rule now regulates agricultural water quality—requiring testing and corrective actions for contamination.

punchline.text: Water touches everything in food production. Dirty water means dirty food.

quiz.question: Why is ice considered a food safety concern?
options: Ice machines are rarely cleaned and can harbor bacteria and biofilms
